newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh says is hopeful about ending insurgency.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh says is hopeful about ending insurgency.

text.p: Bangladesh has made progress in talks with tribal rebel leaders towards ending a 23-year-old insurgency in the southeastern Chittagong Hill Tracts, an official said on Tuesday.

"We have reached a consensus to try all means to solve the problem permanently," Abul Hasanat Abdullah, chief parliamentary whip of the ruling Awami League, said after a meeting with rebel leaders at Khagrachari town, 100 km (60 miles) from Chittagong.
He told reporters the current round of talks, which began on Saturday, had been adjourned until January 25.
"We could be able to draw a draft formula on the solution in the next meeting," he said.

Jyotirindra Budhipriya Larma, chief of the Parbatya Chittagram Jana Sanghati Samity (PCJSS), the political arm of the rebel Shanti Bahini (peace force), said he was satisfied with the progress in the talks.
"The government seems sincere in finding a solution to the problem," he said.

Tribal insurgents have been fighting a bush war for autonomy of 5,500 sq miles (14,200 sq kms) of hill tracts, bordering India and Burma. They also want some 300,000 Bengali-speaking settlers expelled from the area.
Officials say more than 8,500 rebels, soldiers and civilians have been killed in the insurgency since 1973.
A source at the talks said Larma hinted that the rebels would return to normal life "if the government treated them with honour and rehabilitated all of them properly".
On Saturday, the rebel leaders and the government agreed to extend a truce until March 31. The current ceasefire is due to expire on December 31.
